tomato: Give it a stake or cage before it needs one — roots resent disturbance later.
kale: Tolerates a light frost — flavor sweetens after a cold snap.
carrot: Keep the seed bed loose and stone-free so roots grow straight.
onion: Stop watering once tops start to fall over — that is the bulbs curing.
beans: Fixes its own nitrogen — good neighbor for heavy feeders like corn.
lettuce: Bolts in heat — plant early, or tuck it in a taller plant’s shade.
squash: Needs room to sprawl — give it the bed’s edge if space is tight.
basil: Pinch flower spikes to keep leaves coming all season.
pepper: Very tender: set transplants out about two weeks after the last frost.
eggplant: Very tender: wait until about two weeks after the last frost to set it out.
potato: Plant seed potatoes 5–6 inches deep; hill soil up around the stems as they grow.
cucumber: Sow once the soil is warm (about 70°F); a trellis saves space and keeps fruit clean.
zucchini: Sow after the last frost once soil is at least 70°F two inches down.
watermelon: Warm-soil mulch or a low tunnel lets you plant two to three weeks earlier.
melon: Transplants can be harvested up to four weeks earlier than direct-seeded melons.
broccoli: After cutting the main head, side shoots keep coming for weeks.
brussels: Needs a long, cool season — sprouts sweeten after a frost.
collards: Pick the lower leaves as it grows; flavor sweetens after a frost.
cabbage: Set out sturdy five-week-old transplants a few weeks before the last frost.
beet: Each seed is a cluster, so thin the seedlings to about 4 inches.
radish: Ready in about a month — sow every couple of weeks, and again in fall.
spinach: Sow as early as the soil can be worked; it bolts once days turn hot.
chard: Pick the outer leaves and the plant keeps producing all season.
dill: Direct sow only (it hates being transplanted) and resow every two weeks.
parsley: Slow to sprout — expect two to five weeks before seedlings appear.
cilantro: Resow every three to four weeks for steady leaves; it bolts in heat.
garlic: Plant cloves in fall, one to two weeks after the first killing frost.
marigold: Sow outside a week or two after the last frost, or start indoors 4–6 weeks earlier.
borage: Self-sows freely; pick the flowers to keep it blooming.
nasturtium: Lean soil gives more flowers and fewer leaves.
corn: Plant in blocks of at least three or four rows so the wind can pollinate it.
polebean: Needs supports up to 8 feet tall, and yields two to three times what bush beans do.
pea: Sow as soon as the soil stays above 40°F; early plantings yield more.
strawberry: Plant as soon as the soil can be worked, in full sun with good drainage.
artichoke: Start 8–12 weeks before the last frost, and give seedlings a few weeks of cool weather.
